job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

passage: Rohan and his sister Meera were looking at a globe in their living room in Delhi. Meera traced a horizontal circle and asked if it was a painted line on the ground. Rohan laughed and explained that these are imaginary lines called latitudes used for location. He pointed to the vertical lines, the longitudes, which meet at the poles, unlike the parallel latitudes. Meera then asked why the area near the Equator feels so hot. Rohan explained that the Earth is a sphere, and the Sun's rays fall directly on the Torrid Zone, concentrating heat in a small area, not because of the distance to the Sun. They then looked at their watches. Rohan noted that when it is noon in Delhi, it is not noon in London. He explained that as the Earth rotates from west to east, places east of the Prime Meridian see the sunrise earlier. To keep things simple, India follows the 82.5°E longitude as its standard time, which is different from the Prime Meridian. Meera finally understood that time depends on the Earth's rotation, and these lines help us navigate our vast world without needing any physical markings on the planet's surface.

items.evidence: Meera traced a horizontal circle and asked if it was a painted line on the ground. Rohan laughed and explained that these are imaginary lines called latitudes used for location.
items.q: Meera sees a circle on the globe. What is the best way to think of it?
options: An imagined line that helps us find places
A line painted on the ground of Earth
A line cut into the rocks of Earth
A line that shows where the Sun shines
items.explain: Latitudes are imaginary lines used to locate places, not lines drawn on the ground.

wrong.why: thinks latitudes are physical lines on Earth
turns 'physical line' into a marking in the rock
links the lines to the Sun's heat

items.evidence: He pointed to the vertical lines, the longitudes, which meet at the poles, unlike the parallel latitudes.
items.q: How are longitudes different from latitudes on a globe?
options: Longitudes run side by side, never meeting
Longitudes are all of equal length
items.explain: Longitudes are vertical lines that meet at the poles, while latitudes are parallel to each other.

wrong.why: thinks longitudes are parallel like latitudes
mixes up horizontal and vertical lines
thinks all lines have the same length

items.evidence: Rohan explained that the Earth is a sphere, and the Sun's rays fall directly on the Torrid Zone, concentrating heat in a small area, not because of the distance to the Sun.
items.q: Why is the area near the Equator much hotter than other areas?
options: Sunlight strikes it straight and is packed tightly
It sits much nearer to the Sun
The Sun is farther from other places
Its longitudes bring the Sun's heat there
items.explain: The Sun's rays fall directly there, concentrating heat in a small area; the Sun's distance is not the cause.

wrong.why: thinks the Equator is closer to the Sun
thinks the Sun's distance varies by place

items.evidence: He explained that as the Earth rotates from west to east, places east of the Prime Meridian see the sunrise earlier.
items.q: A town lies east of the Prime Meridian. When will its sunrise come?
options: Before sunrise at the Prime Meridian
After sunrise at the Prime Meridian
At the same moment as at the Prime Meridian
Only when it is noon at Delhi
items.explain: Earth rotates west to east, so places east of the Prime Meridian see sunrise earlier.

wrong.why: thinks places east are behind in time
thinks time is the same everywhere
